---
title: Define an agent
description: One definition for what the assistant knows, which tools it may use and which helpers it hands work to. The page and your server read the same file.
sidebar:
  label: 7. Define an agent
---

Your tools say what *can* be done on the page. An **agent** says how: the order the tools go in, what to ask the
person, what to avoid, and which tools are its own. `defineWebAgent` is the one place you write that, the way
`defineWebTool` is the one place you write a tool. It is plain data, so the chat in the browser and your `/api/chat`
route read the same file.

## A complete example

Two agents: `shopper` on every page, and `orders`, a helper it hands questions about past orders to.

Import `defineWebAgent` from `@webmcp-agents/chat/agent`: that entry has no React and no DOM, so a server file can
import it. Install the package if you have not yet:

```package-install
npm install @webmcp-agents/chat
```

## Instructions

`instructions` is a string or a list of lines, added to the system prompt under "About this site". Write what the
model cannot read from the tools: the order of a task ("list_orders before track_order"), which page a tool is on, what to
ask the person, and what never to do. Tool descriptions say what each tool does; instructions say how they fit.

The browser sends only the agent's **id**. The server reads the instructions from its own copy of this file, so page
text never writes your system prompt.

## The tools it may use

Left out, `tools` is every tool on the page. A list narrows it, and takes both kinds of tool, mixed:

- **A catalog tool, by reference**: `tools.getCart`. The object stands for its id.
- **A component's tool, by its id**: `"add_to_cart"`. A tool written with `useWebTool` has no object to import.

The list is an allow-list on both sides: the browser offers the model only these tools, and the server refuses a call
to any other. Listing a catalog tool by reference makes this file import your catalog, which is why catalog files use
`defineWebTool` from `@webmcp-agents/core` and import no React.

A function over the page's tool descriptors works too, for rules a list cannot say:

```ts
tools: (tools) => tools.filter((tool) => tool.name !== "place_order"),
```

## Sub-agents

`agents` gives an agent helpers. Each one becomes a tool named `delegate_to_<id>` (here `delegate_to_orders`) that
takes a `task`. When the parent calls it, the chat runs the helper's own loop, with its own instructions, tools and
model, and hands its final answer back as the tool's result.

- **Write a `description` on a sub-agent.** It becomes the delegate tool's description, which is how the parent knows
  when to call it.
- **A sub-agent sees only the task**, not the parent's conversation, so the parent has to hand over a complete one.
- **It still works the page.** The helper's tools run in the browser under the cursor, and anything confirm-gated
  still waits for the person's click. In the chat, the delegate call shows as a card with the helper's own calls inside
  it.

Register only the top-level agents on the server (the `agents` export above): a sub-agent is found through its parent.
Ids must be unique across the whole tree.

## A model per agent

`model` names the agent's model as `"<provider>/<model>"`. Without it, the agent uses the server's default
(`WEB_AGENTS_MODEL`, else `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`). Give a narrow helper a faster model, as `orders` does.

It is a string, never a key: the server resolves it with the provider's key from its own environment. A provider
other than the default needs its key and its SDK on the server ([Add the chat](/build/add-the-chat#pick-a-model)).

## Use it

The definition is the same wherever the agent runs. The chat takes it as a prop (`<AgentChat agent={shopper} />`,
the next page). To run it with no chat on the page, pick the tab that fits:

<Tabs syncKey="agent-api" hash={false}>
<Tab title="useWebAgent">

In a component, with live status:

```tsx
const agent = useWebAgent(shopper);

<Button onClick={() => agent.invoke("Where is my last order?")}>
  {agent.status === "running" ? "Working…" : "Track my last order"}
</Button>
```

</Tab>
<Tab title="defineWebAgent">

Anywhere else, on the agent itself:

```ts
const { text } = await shopper.invoke("Where is my last order?");
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

[Call an agent](/build/call-an-agent) has both in full.

## Try it

An agent needs a model to run, and the next page adds one: the chat and its `/api/chat` route. Then ask the chat
"Where is my last order?". `shopper` calls `delegate_to_orders`, and the card for it shows the helper going to
`/orders`, calling `list_orders` and then `track_order`.

## Options you'll use most

| Option | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `id` | The agent's name, 1–64 of `a-z A-Z 0-9 _ . -`. The browser sends it; the server looks it up. |
| `instructions` | How the tools fit together: a string or lines. |
| `tools` | The tools it may use: catalog tools and ids, mixed, or a function. Default: every tool on the page. |
| `agents` | Helpers it hands work to, each as a `delegate_to_<id>` tool. |
| `description` | For a sub-agent: what it does, in one sentence. |
| `model` | `"<provider>/<model>"`. Default: the server's. |
| `maxSteps` | Model steps per message for this agent. |

Every option: [`defineWebAgent`](/reference/chat/define-web-agent) and
[`useWebAgent`](/reference/chat/use-web-agent).
